title: 🤖 Hyundai Now Owns Boston Dynamics Outright! The Atlas Robot Is Closing In on Factories!
body: 🤖 Hyundai Now Owns Boston Dynamics Outright! The Atlas Robot Is Closing In on Factories!

Hyundai Motor Group now owns the American robotics company Boston Dynamics outright, after completing the purchase of SoftBank's remaining 9.65% stake, according to a regulatory filing published on 17 November.

Hyundai had bought about 80% of the company in 2021, while SoftBank kept the rest of the stake, until it exercised its sale option last July under an old agreement between the two sides, transferring the shares to group chairman Chung Euisun and its affiliated companies.

The company is valued at about 4.3 trillion Korean won, and analysts say unifying ownership gives Hyundai greater freedom to make decisions and speed up spending on research and production without needing approval from an outside shareholder.

The biggest goal is the humanoid robot Atlas: the group plans to build production capacity of around 30,000 units a year by 2028, starting first at its electric vehicle plant in the US state of Georgia, with simple tasks such as sorting and moving car parts.

Although Boston Dynamics' revenue in the first nine months of the year rose 29% to 136 billion won, its losses widened because of research and production costs, and reports talk of a possible stock market listing for the company around 2029 and 2030.
Simply put: the car company now owns the robotics company outright, and the humanoid robot is getting closer to the production lines — do you think robots will soon be in every factory?
Would you trust a robot working alongside workers in a factory?
